question.problem:
A surveyor stands $15\text{ ft}$ away from the base of a radio tower. An elevator inside the tower moves straight up at a constant speed of $20\text{ ft/s}.$ How fast is the distance between the surveyor and the elevator changing when the elevator is $20\text{ ft}$ above the ground?

The distance between the surveyor and the elevator is
{{field-1}} $\text{ft/s}.$
question.worked_solution:
We start by drawing a diagram of the problem.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14208490/assets/7a6f5b05bc0bd89d01b1b521fa35f4bc613e532a06ce04fea26323e6c5dbbafa.png)

In the diagram,

- $x$ is the distance between the surveyor and the base of the tower,

- $y$ is the distance between the elevator and the ground,

- $z$ is the distance between the surveyor and the elevator.

As shown in the diagram, $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ form a right triangle with $z$ as the hypotenuse. We wish to find the rate of change of $z,$ which is $\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}.$ 

We know that $x=15\,\text{ft}$ and $y=20\,\text{ft}.$ We can find $z$ using the Pythagorean Theorem, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ {15}^{2}+{20}^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ 625 & ={z}^{2} \\ z & =25\,\text{ft}\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that:

- $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=20\,\text{ft}/\text{s},$

- the distance between the surveyor and the base of the tower remains the same, so $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=0.$

Finally, we differentiate both sides of ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}={z}^{2}$ with respect to $t$ and then substitute in the known values, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({z}^{2}) \\ 2x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} \\ 2(15)(0)+2(20)(20) & =2(25)\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} \\ 800 & =50\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the distance between the surveyor and the elevator is $16\,\text{ft}/\text{s}.$
